classification.difficultyReason: The task states that the sheet is curled along the 40 cm side, so the main decisions are scaffolded. The student must see that the 40 cm side becomes the circumference (a rolled-sheet-to-cylinder representation change) and solve 2πr = 40 for r. They must then take the other side, 25 cm, as the height and substitute the exact radius into V = πr²h. This is a short linked chain with an unfamiliar rolling context, but it is more demanding than a direct volume or compare-two-volumes task. It lacks the open comparison of two rolled cylinders in p28-q15 (the 297 mm and 210 mm sheet), which needs reframing and a justified conclusion.

content.prompt:
A rectangular sheet of metal measures $40\text{ cm}$ by $25\text{ cm}$.
It is curled up along its $40\text{ cm}$ side to form a cylinder.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the radius of the cylinder.

answer.worked:
The $40\text{ cm}$ side wraps once around the circular end, so it is the circumference.
$$\begin{align*}C&=2\pi r\\40&=2\pi r\\r&=\frac{40}{2\pi}\\r&=\frac{20}{\pi}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Calculate the volume of the cylinder. Answer to 1 d.p.

answer.worked:
The height of the cylinder is the other side, $25\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}V&=\pi r^2h\\V&=\pi\left(\frac{20}{\pi}\right)^2\times25\\V&=\frac{10\,000}{\pi}\\V&\approx3183.1\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$
